answer: Agents emit a signed pulse every block that includes a proof‑of‑work tied to the physical location of their knoll‑bound compute node; the jetty‑node that aggregates pulses verifies that each proof’s difficulty exceeds a threshold and that the timestamp is within the last epoch. If a node fails to deliver a fresh pulse, its identity score decays to zero and its stake is slashed. An attacker must lock up at least 10 % of the network’s total stake per fake identity and sustain 5 minutes of full‑node work each epoch, costing $150 k of compute and capital per Sybil node.
